en.name: Taro balls, raw
en.summary: Raw taro balls keep 1–2 days in the refrigerator at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 2 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Those numbers are read across from fresh pasta, the closest equivalent — a fresh starch dough with nothing preserving it.
en.pantry: Raw taro balls are little more than mashed taro or sweet potato worked together with starch. There is no salt, no acid and no drying, so they are a fresh dough and belong in the fridge or freezer, not on a worktop. Boiled taro balls are a separate concern: they are a wet cooked starch, and a pot of them sitting in warm syrup at a dessert stall or at home is the Bacillus cereus situation — its spores survive cooking, and poisoning from its toxin is generally associated with rice and other starchy foods. Hold them above 60 °C or chill them to 4 °C (40 °F) or below rather than letting them stand warm.
en.fridge: 1–2 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Keep the raw balls dusted with starch in a single layer on a tray, covered, so they neither dry out nor stick together into a slab. If they have started to go grey and sticky at the surface, boil them now or freeze them, because they will not improve.
en.freezer: 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze them apart on a tray until solid, then bag them — this is the step people skip, and a bagged mass of unfrozen balls welds into one lump. Boil them from frozen, never thawed: a thawed taro ball is a wet lump of dough and it dissolves in the water. Straight into boiling water from the freezer, and they hold their shape and come up chewy.
en.thawing: Do not thaw. Drop frozen taro balls straight into boiling water. Thawed ones fall apart.
spoilage: A sour or fermented smell from the raw dough.
A slimy or sticky surface rather than a dry, starch-dusted one.
Grey, pink or fuzzy spots on the balls.
Balls that dissolve into the water instead of holding shape — a sign they have taken up moisture.
tips: Dust with starch and keep them in a single layer, never piled up.
Freeze on a tray first, then bag; this is the step that matters.
Hold cooked balls above 60 °C or chill them; do not leave them warm in syrup.

faq.q: How long do raw taro balls keep?
faq.a: 1–2 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. That figure is borrowed from fresh pasta rather than published for taro balls.
Yes, 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze them apart on a tray first, then bag them, and boil them straight from frozen.

faq.q: Why do my taro balls dissolve when boiled?
faq.a: They were thawed first, or they had taken up moisture in storage. Boil them from frozen and keep them dusted with starch.

zh.name: 芋圓（生）
zh.summary: 生芋圓冷藏 4 °C 以下可放 1～2 天，冷凍 −18 °C 下 2 個月。這組數字是比照新鮮義大利麵得來的——那是最接近的對應品：一種沒有任何保存處理的新鮮澱粉麵團。
zh.pantry: 生芋圓基本上就是芋頭泥或地瓜泥揉進澱粉，如此而已。沒有鹽、沒有酸、也沒有乾燥，所以它是新鮮麵團，屬於冷藏或冷凍，不屬於流理台。煮熟的芋圓則是另一個問題：那是含水的熟澱粉，而一鍋泡在溫糖水裡、擺在甜品攤或家裡的芋圓，正是仙人掌桿菌的場景——它的孢子撐得過烹煮，而它的毒素造成的中毒，一般都和米飯及其他澱粉類食品有關。請保溫在 60 °C 以上，或冰到 4 °C 以下，不要讓它溫溫地放著。
zh.fridge: 4 °C 以下 1～2 天。生芋圓要沾上薄薄一層澱粉、單層攤在盤子上並蓋好，才不會乾掉、也不會黏成一整片。如果表面已經開始發灰、發黏，就現在煮掉或冷凍，因為它不會變好。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 2 個月。請先攤開在盤子上凍硬，再裝袋——這正是最常被跳過的一步，而直接裝袋的未凍芋圓會黏成一整坨。要煮時直接從冷凍下滾水，絕對不要先解凍：解凍後的芋圓就是一坨濕麵團，一下水就化掉。從冷凍直接下滾水，它才會保持形狀、口感才 Q。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍。冷凍的芋圓直接下滾水。解凍過的會散掉。
spoilage: 生麵團發出酸味或發酵味。
表面變得黏滑，而不是乾爽帶粉。
芋圓上出現灰色、粉紅或絨毛狀的斑點。
下鍋就化在水裡而不是保持形狀——那代表它在保存期間吸了水。
tips: 沾好澱粉、單層排放，不要堆在一起。
先攤盤冷凍再裝袋，這一步最關鍵。
從冷凍直接下滾水，不要解凍。
煮好的芋圓保溫在 60 °C 以上或冰起來，不要溫溫泡在糖水裡。

faq.a: 冷藏 4 °C 以下 1～2 天。這個數字是比照新鮮義大利麵，不是為芋圓公布的。
可以，−18 °C 下 2 個月。先攤盤凍硬再裝袋，並直接從冷凍下滾水。

faq.q: 為什麼我的芋圓一煮就化掉？
faq.a: 因為先解凍了，或保存時吸了水。請沾好澱粉，並從冷凍直接下鍋。
